title: Assembly with Megahit
author: James E Thornton Jr
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kb7csrn
materials: Move into your project directory. $ cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username

steps.title: Log into HPC
steps.instruction: Connect to the high‑performance cluster via SSH (e.g., `ssh hpc.ocelote`).

steps.title: Create and enter assembly directory
steps.instruction: Make a new directory called `assembly` and change into it: `mkdir assembly && cd assembly`.

steps.title: Organize FASTA files
steps.instruction: Create a folder for FASTA files and move all FASTA files into it (adjust paths if needed): `mkdir fasta; mv fastq/*.fasta fasta`.

steps.title: Determine read type
steps.instruction: Check whether you have paired‑end reads (two files per SRR, e.g., *_1.fasta and *_2.fasta) or single‑end reads (one file per SRR). If single‑end, skip to the step for single‑end script; if paired‑end, skip to the step for paired‑end script.

steps.title: Create paired‑end assembly script
steps.instruction:
Create a file named `run-assembly.sh` with the following content (replace `username` with your actual username):
```
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -W group_list=bh_class
#PBS -q windfall
#PBS -l select=1:ncpus=20:mem=40gb
#PBS -l pvmem=38gb
#PBS -l walltime=24:00:00
#PBS -l cput=48:00:00
#PBS -M netid@email.arizona.edu
#PBS -m bea

FASTA_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/fasta'
ASSEM_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly'
MIN_CONTIG_LEN=500
OUT_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly/megahit-out'

cd $ASSEM_DIR
SINGLEs=`ls $FASTA_DIR/*_1.fasta | python -c 'import sys; print ",".join([x.strip() for x in sys.stdin.readlines()])'`
megahit -r $SINGLEs --preset meta-sensitive --min-contig-len $MIN_CONTIG_LEN -o $OUT_DIR -t 12
```
Note: `OUT_DIR` does **not** need to exist beforehand; Megahit will create it automatically.

steps.title: Create single‑end assembly script
steps.instruction:
Create a file named `run-assembly.sh` with the following content (replace `username` with your actual username):
```
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -W group_list=bh_class
#PBS -q windfall
#PBS -l select=1:ncpus=20:mem=40gb
#PBS -l pvmem=38gb
#PBS -l walltime=24:00:00
#PBS -l cput=48:00:00
#PBS -M netid@email.arizona.edu
#PBS -m bea

FASTA_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/fasta'
ASSEM_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly'
MIN_CONTIG_LEN=500
OUT_DIR='/rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly/megahit-out'

cd $ASSEM_DIR
SINGLEs=`ls $FASTA_DIR/*.fasta | python -c 'import sys; print ",".join([x.strip() for x in sys.stdin.readlines()])'`
megahit -r $SINGLEs --preset meta-sensitive --min-contig-len $MIN_CONTIG_LEN -o $OUT_DIR -t 12
```
Again, `OUT_DIR` will be created by Megahit if it does not already exist.

steps.title: Create job output folders
steps.instruction: Make directories for standard output and standard error: `mkdir std-out std-err`.

steps.title: Submit assembly job
steps.instruction:
Make the script executable and submit it to the scheduler, directing output and error to the folders created:
```
chmod +x run-assembly.sh
qsub -e std-err/ -o std-out/ run-assembly.sh
```

steps.title: Monitor job status
steps.instruction: Check the status of your job with `qstat -u username`. Runtime will vary with dataset size.

steps.title: Assess assembly with MetaQuast
steps.instruction: When the job finishes, run MetaQuast on CyVerse to obtain assembly statistics (exact command not provided in the source).

steps.title: Add tools to PATH
steps.instruction: Edit your `.bashrc` file (`nano .bashrc`) and add the line `export PATH=/rsgrps/bh_class/bin:$PATH`. Save the file and reload the shell (`source ~/.bashrc` or log out and back in).
